newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala holds to railway sale deadline.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala holds to railway sale deadline.

text.p: Despite requests from possible bidders to delay the bidding deadline for Guatemala's decaying state-owned railroad, the government hoped to stick to a May 15 date for bids, an official said.

"If we have a firm offer we will stay on time. We don't want to vary from our decisions unless it is indispensable for the process," Gustavo Saravia, the government's privatization and modernization coordinator, told Reuters.
The Guatemalan Railroad Company (Fegua) is scheduled to be the first government company sold off in a massive privatization plan announced earlier this year.

Saravia said seven firms had picked up information about the bidding process and three had completed due diligence -- Canada's Canarail, De-Consult of Germany and a U.S.-Guatemalan joint venture, RDC/Capitales e Inversiones, S.A.
According to Saravia, De-Consult and Canarail both requested the May 15 deadline for offers be postponed.
In recent interviews with local newspapers, Guatemala's transportation minister, Fritz Garcia, said international interest has been low in the exclusive 50-year concession to operate the railroad.
Garcia said Fegua would be a tough sell because of the huge investment the buyer would have to make to improve the line.

The private railroad company will not have to make any downpayment to the government for the concession but is required to commit to rebuilding and repairing Guatemala's 512 miles of rotting, out-of-use railway.
Each bidder must make a set offer of how much it is willing to pay the government annually for the railroad concession.
